Summary description of proposed program (not to exceed 2 pages). Each of the individual course changes as well as this overall program change reflects significant student-focused alterations that strategically and systemically support our adult-learner student population. Included with these documents are our Professional Leadership Studies Curriculum Sheet (track-changed) that indicate the positive impact it will have for our students. Ultimately, we will be providing them with (a) a cohort-style experience with other adult learners, (b) flexibility to craft a learning experience that capitalizes on their professional growth, and (c) courses that offer knowledge-acquisition and skills-development that resonate with the needs of professional workplaces. In summation, the Professional Leadership Studies program changes include: • SPC 211 (Professional Communication) o A new course designed to enhance the professional writing and communication of our Professional Studies students. • SPC 221 (Finance and Budgeting for Professional Workplaces) o A shift in course number a title to entice students from across Professional Studies to take it earlier in their academic journey.

2 • SPC 325 (Socially-Just and Culturally-Relevant Leadership for the Workplace) o A new course that prepares students to effectively lead diverse organizations with a social justice and equity lens. • SPC 335 (Planning and Analysis)—formally SPC 207 o A shift in course number to make it a more advanced course and hopefully attract non-Professional Studies to take it as a 300-level elective. • SPC 490 (Independent Study) o A new course to give both students and faculty an opportunity to craft independent courses that resonate with innovative learning experiences.
For students, they will be able to propose courses not traditionally offered that might propel their growth for work and community engagements, create opportunities for a research project, or explore a specialized interest in professional studies in a deeper, more meaningful way. • SPC 495 (Special Topics) o A new course that provides faculty an outlet to be responsive to learning opportunities that go beyond the traditional curriculum.
The “Special Topics” seminar is devised to be utilized for courses that address contemporary topics, problems, and issues that our professional workplaces face.

Additionally, course this will enable us to craft new learning experiences in international contexts (e.g., “Comparative Leadership: Taiwan and the USA” or “International NGO and Social Sector Impact in the Dominican Republic”) that are not traditionally offered within the curriculum.
Overall, these changes will install a cohort-style experience by encouraging students from across Professional Studies to take three 200-level courses (i.e., SPC 201, 211, and 221) together at the start of the academic journey.
Similarly, they will take SPC 499 as a Professional Studies-wide culminating educational experience.
These four courses are intended to be required for the Professional Leadership Studies degree.
Students will then have the option of taking other PLS-approved SPC courses to secure their remaining eighteen major credits.
This may include the traditional courses (SPC 215, 325, 335, 401, 420, 450), an internship experience for up to six credits (SPC 480), or an Independent Study / Special Topics for up to six credits (SPC 490, 495). 6.
